## Resulting person body

```markdown
# Morgan Hale

Morgan's known context here is failure-log review: in the reliability review,
Morgan described investigating failures and deciding whether to release.
[[meetings/reliability-review|Reliability review · lines 3–4]]

## State

### Release

Morgan is holding the release until two failure cases are understood.
[[meetings/reliability-review|Reliability review · lines 3–4]]

### Open commitments

Morgan will send a failure report; no deadline set.
[[meetings/reliability-review|Reliability review · line 5]]
```

The introduction says how Morgan is known and State holds the current situation
by topic. What happened at the review is the body of Morgan's `attended`
relationship to the meeting, "Reported two failure cases and committed to a
failure report.", which becomes the review's row in Morgan's derived Timeline.

## Updating the same profile after a later review

Assume a second retained transcript is returned at
`meetings/reliability-follow-up.md`, with resolved Morgan identity:

```text
1  Meeting: Reliability follow-up
2  Date: 2026-09-25. Attendee: Morgan Hale. Speaker mapping: Morgan = Morgan Hale.
3  Morgan: I sent the failure report this morning. Both cases are understood now.
4  Morgan: I approved the release. Deployment has not happened yet.
```

Both State topics change, so rewrite them in place:

```markdown
## State

### Release

Morgan approved the release after both failure cases were understood; it has not
deployed yet. [[meetings/reliability-follow-up|Reliability follow-up · lines 3–4]]

### Open commitments

None; the failure report was sent.
[[meetings/reliability-follow-up|Reliability follow-up · line 3]]
```

The follow-up gets its own `attended` relationship, "Sent the failure report and
approved the release.", so Morgan's Timeline shows both meetings without a page
edit. The introduction need not change. A page rewrite does not change the separate
commitment claim; follow publication guidance for that.
